conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I’ll be your doctor during this stay. Can you tell me what happened with your hip?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Hi, yes. I fell a few days ago and had hip pain. It got a little better, but then suddenly got worse again. I can’t walk on it now.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You also mentioned feeling weak and some blurry vision. Any fevers or chills?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No fevers. I just feel cold sometimes. My hands have been shaky since the fall.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. We’ve reviewed your CT scan. You have a fracture in your right hip — the acetabulum — and there’s some concern about fluid in the joint. Given your history of joint infections, we need to check if this could be infected.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Oh no. I had that knee infection before. Could this be the same thing?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s possible, but not certain. That’s why orthopedics wants to do a joint aspiration — take a small sample of fluid to test for infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will it hurt? I’m already in so much pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll do it with imaging guidance and use numbing medicine. It may be uncomfortable, but we’ll make sure you’re as comfortable as possible.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay, I trust you. What about my kidneys? My creatinine was up last time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good question. Your transplant team is involved. Your ultrasound today showed your transplanted kidney looks stable. No signs of rejection or blockage.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s a relief. But my energy is so low. Is it the anemia again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, your hemoglobin was low — 7.1 — so we gave you two units of blood in the ER. It’s now 8.4. We think it’s from both your kidney disease and the hematoma from the fall.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ve been on epo at home. Should I keep that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, you’ll continue that as an outpatient. We’re also watching your acid levels. Your bicarbonate was low, so we’re adjusting your sodium bicarbonate dose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. And my blurry vision — should I be worried?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your CT head didn’t show any new bleeding or stroke. The changes are old, from your prior stroke. But we’ll keep an eye on it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. We tried to do the hip aspiration yesterday with CT guidance, but it had to be stopped because you were in too much pain to lie still.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’m so sorry. It was unbearable. Can we try again?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes. Ortho and radiology are planning to use fluoroscopy instead, and we’ll give more pain control beforehand. We need that fluid to rule out infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I understand. I don’t want another joint infection like my knee.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Exactly. And if it is infected, we’ll need to act quickly. But so far, you haven’t had a fever, and your white count is normal — that’s reassuring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, we’re set to do the hip aspiration today with fluoroscopy. You’ll get pain meds first. Any questions?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Will I be awake? I’m nervous.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’ll be awake but sedated and numbed at the site. You’ll feel pressure, but not sharp pain. We’ll be right there the whole time.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We just finished the procedure. It went well. They got a small amount of fluid — less than 1 cc — and it’s been sent for culture and gram stain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. Does that mean the fracture is new?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Actually, ortho reviewed the imaging and thinks the fracture is chronic — it’s been there a while. There’s no new callus formation, and there’s bone resorption. The fall may have worsened it.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: So no surgery? What now?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: For now, you must stay non-weight-bearing on that leg. No putting any weight on it. Ortho will decide next steps after we get the culture results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your transplant team also reviewed your meds. We’re lowering your tacrolimus from 5 mg to 4 mg twice a day. Your level was 5.5 on admission, now 4.3 — still in range.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Is that safe? I don’t want to lose the kidney.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: It’s safe. Your level is still therapeutic. We’re adjusting it because your kidney function is slowly declining — your creatinine is 2.7 now, down from 3.1.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And the sodium bicarbonate? You changed that too.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we reduced it to 650 mg twice a day. Your bicarbonate level improved, so we’re tapering it to avoid side effects.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good news — your blood cultures are negative. No sign of bloodstream infection.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: That’s great. What about the hip fluid?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Still pending. It takes up to a week. But you’ve had no fever, normal WBC, and low inflammatory markers — so infection seems unlikely.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Physical therapy evaluated you. You need two people to help you pivot or move. They strongly recommend rehab.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I know, but I want to go home. I have help there.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We understand, but it’s risky. If you put weight on that hip, it could displace further. Falls are also a real concern.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I promise I won’t walk on it. My daughter will help me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. We’ll discharge you home with services. But you must follow up with ortho in two weeks for the culture results.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my kidney doctor?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, see them next week. They’ll check your tacrolimus level and discuss your dialysis access. You’re scheduled for fistula placement soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Today’s the day. Your labs are stable. Hemoglobin is 8.0, creatinine 2.7. You’re ready to go home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. What about pain meds?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re going home with OxyContin 20 mg twice a day and Oxycodone 5 mg every 4 hours as needed. Only a three-day supply. Please don’t overuse them.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I won’t. I remember what happened last time with tramadol.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good. And remember — no weight on that right leg. Use your walker. Follow up with ortho and nephrology. Call us if you develop fever, increased pain, or swelling.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for taking such good care of me.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: You’re welcome. Take care, and we’ll see you in follow-up.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Just a final check before discharge. Any new symptoms? Pain, dizziness, vision changes?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: No, I feel about the same. Still shaky, but that’s been going on since the fall.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Okay. Neuro says it’s likely from your old stroke. We’ll keep monitoring.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: And my blurry vision?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Still likely related to your prior stroke. But if it worsens, see your eye doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Got it. I’m ready when you are.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ll get the discharge papers ready. Home health will contact you today.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you again, Doctor.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take care. We’re here if you need us.
